title: Air-fryer crab cakes
subtitle: Crab meat patties with a panko crust, air-fried until golden.
excerpt: White crab meat bound with a little mayonnaise, lemon, and herbs, pressed into patties and coated in panko breadcrumbs, then air-fried until golden and crisp. Makes four cakes. Serves two.
sourceNotes: Crab cakes are a preparation found across British coastal cooking and in American East Coast cuisine. The air fryer produces a crisp outer coating without the risk of the patties breaking apart in oil, as the cakes hold their shape in the basket.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before cooking on a lined tray, then transfer to bags. Cook from frozen at 190°C for 16 minutes, flipping halfway.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the recipe and freeze half before cooking.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shape and refrigerate for up to 8 hours before cooking.

content.text: Crab cakes need enough binder to hold together without masking the crab. Too much filler and the crab becomes an afterthought. Use just enough mayonnaise to bring the mixture together when squeezed. Chilling the shaped patties for 30 minutes before cooking firms them up and stops them breaking apart in the basket.

items.prepNote: white crab meat, drained of any liquid

content.text: Pick through {{crab-meat}} of crab meat and remove any shell fragments. Combine with {{mayonnaise}} of mayonnaise, 40 g of panko, {{spring-onion}} of sliced spring onion, the zest and juice of half the {{lemon}}, {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard, and {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt. Mix gently ,  do not overwork or the crab will become paste. Divide into four and shape into patties about 2 cm thick. Coat each patty in the remaining 60 g of panko, pressing to adhere. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Preheat the air fryer to 190°C. Spray the basket and both sides of each patty with cooking oil. Cook for 6 minutes, flip carefully with a spatula, and cook for a further 5-6 minutes until golden all over. Serve with the remaining lemon cut into wedges.

items.cause: Not chilled long enough, or mixture too wet.
items.fix: Chill for the full 30 minutes. If the crab meat was very wet, squeeze it in a clean cloth to remove excess moisture before mixing.
Spray generously. Panko breadcrumbs need oil to crisp; without it they stay dusty and pale.
Cook at 190°C, not 200°C. The lower temperature gives the centre time to heat through before the outside burns.

content.text: Air-fryer crab cakes are a good starter for a seafood meal. Serve with a small salad of dressed watercress, a wedge of lemon, and a dollop of tartare sauce or aioli. They also work as a light main with new potatoes and a green salad.
